A character who is not attacking blocks attacks, blaster bolts and thrown lightsabers that come from within the character's block arc. The block arc is the area in front of the character where blocks are possible. The arc is wider at a higher defense level. It is also wider against blades than against bolts. A character with no defense level does not block.

A character blocks an attack when the cosine of the angle between the attack and the character's facing is above a limit. The limit is 0.9 at defense level 1, 0.6 at level 2 and 0.3 at level 3. A lower limit means a wider arc.

A character with a lightsaber blocks blaster bolts at a bolt level. The bolt level starts at the character's defense level. The lightsaber's deflection bonus raises or lowers it. The bolt level is 1 lower while the character jumps or moves backward. At bolt level 1 the blade absorbs the bolt. At level 2 the blade deflects the bolt in the direction the character is looking. At level 3 the blade reflects the bolt back at the shooter.

An NPC who deflects blaster bolts in quick succession can be overwhelmed. Every bolt the NPC deflected in the last 2 seconds counts toward the Overwhelmed rule. This applies under both the Jedi Academy rules and the Advanced rules.

For every bolt an NPC deflected in the last 2 seconds, the next bolt has a chance to get past the NPC's lightsaber and hit them. The chance for each deflected bolt is 16% with Jedi Defense, 12% with Advanced Jedi Defense and 8% with Master Jedi Defense. An NPC without the feat has a chance of 20% for each bolt. The first bolt after a pause is always deflected as usual.

A bolt that an NPC deflects strays further from where the NPC sent it. It strays by up to 0.2 on each axis with Jedi Defense, 0.15 with Advanced Jedi Defense and 0.1 with Master Jedi Defense. An NPC without the feat makes it stray by up to 0.25. This applies under both the Jedi Academy rules and the Advanced rules.

When the blocker's defense level equals the level of the throw, the blocker knocks the lightsaber to the ground with a chance of 4 in 10.

When a character has ranks in Demolitions, a found mine offers the actions Disarm Mine and Recover Mine. Disarming a mine takes 4.5 seconds. In combat, the character rolls Demolitions + 1d20. Out of combat, the character uses Demolitions + 20 instead of a roll. The mine is disarmed if this total equals or beats the mine's disarm DC. A mine with a disarm DC above 35 can never be disarmed. If the total falls short of the DC by more than 10, the mine goes off.

Disarming or recovering a mine takes 4.5 seconds.

A character can disarm or recover a mine from up to 3 meters from its center. The character stands outside the mine's edge, which is 1.5 meters from its center.

A mine with a disarm DC above 35 can never be disarmed.

If a check to disarm a mine falls short of the DC by more than 10, the mine goes off.

Recovering a mine works like disarming it, but the DC is 10 higher. If the check falls short of the DC by more than 5, the mine goes off. A recovered mine goes into the party's inventory.

The DC to recover a mine is the disarm DC +10.

If a check to recover a mine falls short of the DC by more than 5, the mine goes off.

Set Mine places the most powerful mine in the party's inventory. Setting a mine takes 2 seconds, and the character must stand still. The check is made the same way as for disarming, against the mine's set DC. A character with 5 or more ranks in Demolitions gains a +2 bonus. The total of the check is added to the mine's own detection and disarm DCs, so a well-set mine is harder to find and to disarm. The party may have at most 15 mines set in one area.

Setting a mine takes 2 seconds. In TSL, setting a mine on a door takes the same time.

The party may have at most 15 mines set in one area.

A character with 5 or more ranks in Demolitions gains a bonus to set mines. Only ranks bought with skill points count, not bonuses from items or attributes.

A character with enough ranks in Demolitions gains a +2 bonus to set mines.

In combat, a check to set a mine that falls short by more than 10 still sets the mine.

In TSL, a character can set a mine on a locked door or a locked object, unless the game's data says that the lock cannot be blasted. No die is rolled, even in combat. The mine explodes 3 seconds after it is set. The blast's strength is 20, plus the setter's Demolitions divided by 2 for a door or by 20 for an object, plus the mine's own blast strength. If this total equals or beats the lock's DC, the lock opens. A blasted object is unlocked at once. A blasted door is unlocked and swings open 1 second after the blast.

A mine's blast against a door's lock adds the setter's Demolitions divided by 2, rounded down.

A mine's blast against a locked object, such as a footlocker, adds the setter's Demolitions divided by 20, rounded down.

A skill check is a d20 roll plus the character's skill total, against a difficulty class (DC). The check succeeds if the result is equal to or higher than the DC. Out of combat, the character does not roll, and the roll counts as 20.

Skill checks, attack rolls, critical hits and saving throws are rolled on a d20.

Out of combat, a skill check counts as a roll of 20.

In KOTOR 2, every lock has a difficulty level as well as a DC. A lock of difficulty level 0, 1 or 2 has a DC of 21 plus the lock's own modifier. The game ignores the DC written on the lock. Security checks and the blast of a mine both use this DC. KOTOR 1 always uses the DC written on the lock.

In KOTOR 2, a lock of difficulty level 3 becomes harder as the player gains levels. Its DC is the DC of a level 0 to 2 lock, plus the lock's own modifier, plus 7, plus the player's level.

A KOTOR 2 lock of difficulty level 3 adds 7 and the player's level to its DC.

A KOTOR 2 lock of difficulty level 4 uses the DC written on the lock, like every lock in KOTOR 1.

Using Security, disarming or recovering a mine, and laying a mine all take time. The attempt is cancelled if the character moves more than 0.5 meters, attacks or falls.

A skill use in progress is cancelled if the character moves more than 0.5 meters.

In KOTOR 2, the party gains experience when a party member disarms a mine, recovers a mine, or opens a lock with the Security skill. The experience is a multiple of the main character's level. A mine or a lock is hard when its DC is at least the main character's level + 20.

A mine or a lock counts as hard when its DC is at least the main character's level + 20.

In KOTOR 2, disarming or recovering a mine gives 10 times the main character's level, or 15 times the level for a hard mine.

A character walking to disarm or recover a mine stops beside the mine, never on it. The character stops 0.6 meters outside the mine's edge, which is 1.5 meters from its center.

A character walking to a mine counts as arrived once it is within 0.7 meters of the spot where it should stop. The character comes to a full stop there before it acts.

A character with Force Camouflage and no ranks in Stealth counts as having 1 rank.

To enter Stealth Mode, a character needs ranks in the Stealth skill and a stealth unit equipped. A character cannot enter Stealth Mode during combat. A character in Stealth Mode cannot run, unless the character knows Stealth Run. Stealth Mode ends when the character attacks, uses a Force power, throws a grenade, enters combat, removes the stealth unit or starts a conversation.

An attack that hits within 1.5 seconds after the character leaves Stealth Mode is a sneak attack. This only works against a target that has not yet noticed the attacker.

A character in Stealth Mode, or wearing an item with Special Walk, can only walk. A character in Stealth Mode who knows Stealth Run may run, but an item with Special Walk still holds the character to a walk. The walk is 64 out of 127 on the movement scale, where 127 is a full run.

Each character rolls a Stealth roll against sight and a second Stealth roll against hearing. Each of these rolls is 10 plus a random number from 1 to 10. Each character also rolls a spot roll and a listen roll, and each of these is a random number from 1 to 20. All four rolls are made again every 20 seconds.

A character keeps its Stealth, spot and listen rolls for 20 seconds. Then it rolls them again.

A Stealth roll is 10 plus a random number from 1 to 10.

A Stealth roll adds a random number from 1 to 10 to its base.

An opponent sees a character in Stealth Mode within its line of sight if the opponent's Awareness plus its spot roll is higher than the character's Stealth skill plus its Stealth roll. The opponent suffers -5 to the check while it runs. It suffers -10 while it is in combat. An enemy suffers -5 when a player's character is behind it. The opponent suffers -5 if the character is standing still. The opponent gains +5 while it is standing still itself. Distance also lowers the check. The first 2 steps of 3 meters are free, and every further 3 meters is -1.

An enemy suffers -5 to its spot check against a player's character who is behind it.

A character counts as behind an opponent when the cosine of the angle between the opponent's facing and the direction to the character is -0.707 or less. With the standard value, this is the quarter circle directly behind the opponent.

When a character in Stealth Mode stands still, the opponent suffers -5 to its spot check.

Every 3 meters of distance is -1 to the spot check, except for the first few steps (see Spot Distance Free).

The first 2 steps of 3 meters of distance cause no penalty to the spot check.

An opponent hears a character in Stealth Mode within its hearing if the opponent's Awareness plus its listen roll is higher than the character's Stealth skill plus its Stealth roll. Every 3 meters of distance is -1 to the check. Each meter of wall between them is -5 to the check. Large creatures are easier to hear, and small ones are harder to hear. Some areas raise or lower all listen checks.

Every 3 meters of distance is -1 to the listen check.

A creature's size changes the listen check against it. From Tiny to Huge, the change is -8 points / -4 points / 0 points / 4 points / 8 points.

Each meter of wall between the opponent and the character is -5 to the listen check.

Some areas award experience for getting through them unseen. Each time a hostile creature spots a party member, the area lowers this award by a set amount. The award drops 6 seconds after the creature sees the party member. It drops at once if the creature attacks a party member before then.

The area's stealth experience award drops 6 seconds after a hostile creature sees a party member.

Each character also rolls a spot roll and a listen roll, and each of these is a random number from 1 to 20. All four rolls are made again every 20 seconds.

An active creature checks what it can see and hear at random intervals. Each wait lasts at least 0.3 seconds, plus up to 0.4 seconds more. A creature in a conversation checks only every 4 seconds. A creature checks what it hears before it checks what it sees.

An active creature waits at least 0.3 seconds between checks of what it can see and hear.

Each wait between perception checks lasts up to 0.4 seconds longer, at random.

A creature in a conversation checks what it can see and hear every 4 seconds.

Every creature searches for hidden mines every 0.1 seconds. A creature searches up to 20 meters beyond the edge of a mine, and a mine's edge is 1.5 meters from its center. The creature finds the mine if its Awareness + 1d10 + 10 equals or beats the mine's detection DC. A running character suffers a -5 penalty to this check.

Every creature searches for mines every 0.1 seconds. The search is always active, and the player never has to start it.

A creature can find a mine from up to 20 meters beyond the mine's edge.

An Awareness check to find a mine adds +10 to the roll.

An Awareness check to find a mine rolls 1d10.

A running character suffers a -5 penalty to Awareness checks to find mines.

Each rank in Treat Injury (or Repair for droids) speeds up medpac / repair kit use by 0.1 seconds.

Droids only. Restores 15 (Repair Kit), 25 (Advanced), or 35 (Construction Kit) Vitality, plus your Intelligence mod and +1 / +2 / +3 per rank in Repair.

At a workbench, a character can break items down into components and build new items from components. A lab station works the same way with chemicals. Each item has a price in components, which is worked out from its value and is at least 1. Building the item costs that price. Breaking the item down returns that price, or less if the character's skill is low.

A party member can revive an unconscious ally by standing still beside it and holding [Use]. A revive takes 3 seconds. Each rank the reviver has in Treat Injury takes 0.1 seconds off that time. When the unconscious ally is a droid, the reviver's ranks in Repair count instead. A revive never takes less than 1 second.

Each rank in Treat Injury takes 0.1 seconds off the time a revive takes. When the unconscious ally is a droid, ranks in Repair count instead.

A revive always takes at least 1 second.

A locked door or container opens if a party member has its key. Otherwise a character can use the Security skill, which takes 1.5 seconds. The character makes a Security check, adds the bonus of the security spike used, and compares the result with the lock's DC. The spike is used up only if the attempt fails.

Using Security on a lock takes 1.5 seconds.

When taking 20 does not open a lock of DC 60 or more, the message Impossible appears.
